description:
fz-sc8.16 builds OptionParser.parse/2 with strict: and aliases:. Not built, by agreement: switches: (non-strict, creates atoms), :regex, return_separator:, allow_nonexistent_atoms:, parse!/2, parse_head/2, parse_head!/2, next/2, to_argv/2, split/1 and error formatting. Each as in Elixir 1.19.4, checked with oracle fixtures.

Two differences .16 left, to close here: (1) an unknown one-letter alias consumes the next token in Elixir whatever the atom table holds ('-t 5' with no aliases: gives {[], [], [{"-t", nil}]}), while fz's text lookup leaves it ({[], ["5"], [{"-t", nil}]}); the strict-name rule (an unknown --name never consumes) stays. (2) a multi-letter alias key (aliases: [abc: :x], then -abc) works but prints none of Elixir's deprecation warning on stderr.
title: OptionParser's remaining surface
